result.markdown: --- title: "Session 5 — Sensitivity Analysis and Reporting" subtitle: "Unmeasured confounding · E-value · benchmarks · positivity · target trial · reporting · Lab 5" author: "Community Medicine Workshop" format: revealjs: theme: serif css: [../assets/slide_deck.css, assets/workshop.css, assets/quiz.css] include-after-body: assets/quiz-include.html embed-resources: true slide-number: true navigation-mode: linear code-copy: true center: false transition: fade width: 1280 height: 720 fig-align: center html-math-method: plain execute: echo: true warning: false message: false fig-width: 9 fig-height: 4.6 fig-dpi: 100 --- ## Where we are ::: {.incremental} - Sessions 2 to 4: four methods, one answer (about −6 mmHg) - All assume **no unmeasured confounding**. Today: **how fragile** is the conclusion? - By the end you can: - compute and interpret an **E-value** - **benchmark** it against measured confounders - frame the study as a **target trial** and **report** it ::: # Topic 1 — Unmeasured confounding {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## The untestable assumption ::: {.warn} In these data an **unrecorded** factor, **motivation**, raises enrolment and lowers SBP. No method can adjust for it. That is why the estimates are **−6.3** where the truth is **−5.8**: a small **residual bias**. In real data you **never know** its size; you can only ask **how strong** it would have to be. ::: ## A risk ratio for a binary outcome ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} round(rr, 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` RR lo hi 1.57 1.44 1.71 ``` ::: ::: Controlled BP at 12 months (SBP below 140): **RR 1.57** (95% CI 1.44 to 1.71), adjusted for the confounders. A Poisson model with **robust SE** gives a **risk ratio** for a common outcome (A2). ## The E-value ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} evalues.RR(est = rr[["RR"]], lo = rr[["lo"]], hi = rr[["hi"]]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` point lower upper RR 1.572550 1.443493 1.713146 E-values 2.521425 2.243604 NA ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} **E-value 2.5** (and **2.2** for the confidence limit). An unmeasured confounder would need a risk ratio of **at least 2.5 with both enrolment and BP control**, beyond the measured confounders, to **explain the effect away**; **2.2** would be enough to make the CI include 1. **Large E-value = robust**; close to 1 = fragile. ::: ## Is 2.5 plausible? Benchmarks ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} round(exp(coef(m_rr))[c("diabetes", "educationSecondary+", "urban")], 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` diabetes educationSecondary+ urban 0.70 1.23 1.06 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} round(c(full = coef(m_adj)[["programme"]], without_baseline_sbp = coef(update(m_adj, . ~ . - baseline_sbp))[["programme"]]), 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` full without_baseline_sbp -6.29 -3.38 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - The **measured** confounders have risk ratios of **0.70** (diabetes; 1.43 inverted), **1.23** and **1.06**: none is near **2.5** - Leaving out **baseline SBP**, the strongest one, moves the estimate from **−6.3 to −3.4**: it does **not** remove it - So an unmeasured confounder **strong enough** to cancel the effect is **unlikely**; one that **shifts it somewhat** is **plausible** - The E-value is **not** a p-value and has **no threshold**: interpret it with **subject knowledge** ::: # Topic 2 — Design thinking {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Other threats | Threat | Check | |---|---| | **Positivity** violated | propensity scores near 0 or 1 (here 3 below 0.05, 3 above 0.95) | | **Time zero** unclear, immortal time | define eligibility, start of follow-up and exposure **at the same moment** | | **Selection** (loss to follow-up) | compare those lost; weights for censoring | | **Measurement error** in confounders | residual confounding | | **Model misspecification** | flexible terms (A6), doubly robust | ## Emulate a target trial ::: {.good} Write the **trial you would have liked to run**, then copy it with the data: 1. **Eligibility** (who, when) 2. **Strategies** compared (enrol vs usual care) 3. **Assignment** (emulated by adjusting for baseline confounders) 4. **Start of follow-up** (= eligibility = assignment) 5. **Outcome** and follow-up 6. **Causal contrast** (ATE, ATT; intention-to-treat or per-protocol) 7. **Analysis plan** ::: # Topic 3 — Reporting {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## What to report ::: {.good} - The **causal question**, the **estimand** and the **DAG** (supplement) - **Confounders** and why; **what was not** adjusted for (mediators, colliders) - The **method**, **balance** (table or love plot), **overlap**, weights or matches dropped - **Estimate with CI** from the main method, and the others as **sensitivity** - **E-value** or other bias analysis; **limitations** - Use careful words: "**estimated effect under the assumption of no unmeasured confounding**" ::: ::: {.key} *Example:* "After adjustment for age, sex, education, residence, BMI, diabetes and baseline SBP, enrolment was associated with a 6.3 mmHg lower SBP at 12 months (95% CI 5.4 to 7.1); matching (−5.9) and weighting (−5.7) gave similar estimates. The E-value for BP control was 2.5 (2.2 for the confidence limit)." ::: ## 🔧 Switch to R — Lab 5 {.lab-slide background-color="#1565c0"} ::: {.lab-box} **File:** `causal-workshop/labs/lab5_sens.R` - risk ratio for BP control and its E-value - benchmarks: measured confounders, leave-one-out - positivity check and a reporting sentence ::: **Time:** 35 minutes · answer the Q questions in the comments ## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="z5q1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="kv3p7m.g09pv1" data-show="VGhlIG1ldGhvZCBkb2VzIG5vdCBkcml2ZSB0aGUgcmVzdWx0LCBidXQgYWxsIHNoYXJlIG9u ZSBhc3N1bXB0aW9u" data-explain="VGhlIG1ldGhvZHMgdXNlIHRoZSBzYW1lIG1lYXN1cmVkIGNvbmZvdW5kZXJzIGluIGRpZmZl cmVudCB3YXlzLiBUaGVpciBhZ3JlZW1lbnQgcnVsZXMgb3V0IG1ldGhvZC1zcGVjaWZpYyBw cm9ibGVtcywgbm90IHVubWVhc3VyZWQgY29uZm91bmRpbmcu"} Regression, matching and weighting all give about -6 mmHg. What does this agreement show? - The estimate is free of confounding, as three methods confirm the same value - The method does not drive the result, but all share one assumption - Unmeasured confounding is absent, or else the methods would disagree - The programme works equally well in each subgroup of adults in the cohort ::: ## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="z5q2" data-type="mcq" data-hash="kv42gd.g0a4cg" data-show="QSBoaWRkZW4gY29uZm91bmRlciBuZWVkcyBhIHJpc2sgcmF0aW8gb2YgMi41IHdpdGggZXhw b3N1cmUgYW5kIG91dGNvbWUgdG8gY2FuY2VsIHRoZSBlZmZlY3Q=" data-explain="VGhlIEUtdmFsdWUgaXMgdGhlIG1pbmltdW0gc3RyZW5ndGggb2YgYXNzb2NpYXRpb24sIHdp dGggYm90aCB0aGUgZXhwb3N1cmUgYW5kIHRoZSBvdXRjb21lLCB0aGF0IGFuIHVubWVhc3Vy ZWQgY29uZm91bmRlciB3b3VsZCBuZWVkIHRvIGZ1bGx5IGFjY291bnQgZm9yIHRoZSBlc3Rp bWF0ZS4="} The E-value for the risk ratio is 2.5. What does it mean? - There is a 2.5% probability that the effect is due to unmeasured confounding in the data - The true risk ratio is 2.5 once the unmeasured confounding has been removed from the estimate - An unmeasured confounder with a risk ratio of 2.5 has been shown to exist in these data - A hidden confounder needs a risk ratio of 2.5 with exposure and outcome to cancel the effect ::: ## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="z5q3" data-type="mcq" data-hash="kv4foz.g0aitq" data-show="Q29tcGFyZSBpdCB3aXRoIHRoZSBzdHJlbmd0aCBvZiB0aGUgbWVhc3VyZWQgY29uZm91bmRl cnM=" data-explain="VGhlcmUgaXMgbm8gdGhyZXNob2xkLiBJZiB0aGUgc3Ryb25nZXN0IGtub3duIGNvbmZvdW5k ZXJzIGFyZSBtdWNoIHdlYWtlciB0aGFuIHRoZSBFLXZhbHVlLCBhbiB1bm1lYXN1cmVkIG9u ZSBvZiB0aGF0IHN0cmVuZ3RoIGlzIGxlc3MgcGxhdXNpYmxlLg=="} How can you judge whether an E-value of 2.5 is reassuring? - Compare it with the strength of the measured confounders - Check whether it is larger than the conventional threshold of 2 - Check whether its p-value is below 0.05 in the output - Compare it with the E-values of other variables in the same model ::: ## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="z5q4" data-type="mcq" data-hash="kv4sxq.g0axb5" data-show="VG8gZGVmaW5lIGVsaWdpYmlsaXR5LCB0aW1lIHplcm8gYW5kIHN0cmF0ZWdpZXMgYXMgYSB0 cmlhbCB3b3VsZA==" data-explain="U3BlY2lmeWluZyB0aGUgaHlwb3RoZXRpY2FsIHRyaWFsIGZvcmNlcyBhIGNsZWFyIHF1ZXN0 aW9uIGFuZCBhbGlnbnMgZWxpZ2liaWxpdHksIHN0YXJ0IG9mIGZvbGxvdy11cCBhbmQgZXhw b3N1cmUsIHdoaWNoIHByZXZlbnRzIGJpYXNlcyBzdWNoIGFzIGltbW9ydGFsIHRpbWUu"} What is the purpose of emulating a target trial? - To replace the observational data by simulated data from a trial - To make the confidence intervals as narrow as those of a real trial - To define eligibility, time zero and strategies as a trial would - To remove the need to measure and adjust for the confounders ::: ## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="z5q5" data-type="mcq" data-hash="kv566e.g0bbsh" data-show="QW4gZXN0aW1hdGVkIGVmZmVjdCwgYXNzdW1pbmcgbm8gdW5tZWFzdXJlZCBjb25mb3VuZGlu Zw==" data-explain="VGhlIGFuYWx5c2lzIHRhcmdldHMgYSBjYXVzYWwgZWZmZWN0IGFuZCBzaG91bGQgc2F5IHNv LCB0b2dldGhlciB3aXRoIHRoZSBhc3N1bXB0aW9ucyBvbiB3aGljaCB0aGF0IGludGVycHJl dGF0aW9uIHJlc3RzLg=="} Which wording is appropriate when reporting an observational causal analysis? - A proven causal effect, since the confounders were adjusted for - An estimated effect, assuming no unmeasured confounding - An association, since causal language is not allowed without a trial - An effect that holds for each individual adult who enrolled ::: ## Score and take-home **Your score: ** ::: {.incremental} - All methods assume **no unmeasured confounding** - **E-value**: how strong must a hidden confounder be? - **Benchmark** against measured confounders - Think **target trial**: eligibility, time zero, strategies - Report **estimand, DAG, balance, sensitivity** and careful wording ::: **Next:** Cheat sheet; the advanced series is complete

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
